what: Deploy of main f3f1a76 (the merge of PR #130: the API keeps idle keep-alive connections for 180 s, longer than Caddy reuses them) to the public pilot, and its verification. Also a read-only identification of the unattached PostgreSQL volume reported on 2026-11-15.

The landing page returned 502 twice (06:03:36 and 06:03:38) when the web container was recreated.

route_correctness: Every route answer checked after the deploy matched the recorded journey: 401.3 m with 3 stairways (standard) against 503.7 m with none (wheelchair), dataset 51585450, ml_predictions_used false. That is both smoke runs and all 25 gapped public routes below.

idle_close_inside_the_container.method: one GET /api/v1/health/live over HTTP/1.1 keep-alive on 127.0.0.1:8000 inside the API container, then wait for the server to close the idle connection (idle_close.py)

public_gapped_routes.method: laptop, through Caddy, one request at a time: the smoke journey after idle gaps either side of the old 5 s timeout and up to 60 s, every answer checked (gapped_routes.py)

caddy_upstream_connections.method: local ports of Caddy's established connections to :8000, read every second in Caddy's network namespace, 06:07:02–06:12:46 (caddy_conns.sh)
caddy_upstream_connections.reading: One connection stayed open through the whole window and carried every route from 06:07:42 on, across idle gaps of up to 60 s. The other three, opened by the host smoke run's parallel requests about two minutes earlier, closed together at 06:07:32: Caddy's two-minute idle timeout, not the API's.

caddy_log_after_ready.note: the two 429s are the smoke runs' own rate-limit checks

caddy_log_during_switch.note: the switch itself: the API container replaced, then the graph loading; 499 is a client that gave up

keep_alive_fix.limit: Five minutes cannot show a rare race is gone: the one upstream reset in Caddy's log came after about 40,000 requests. What this shows is the mechanism: the API no longer closes a connection Caddy may still reuse.

other_502s_in_caddy_log: Besides the 2026-11-15 23:30:19 route 502 (the race), Caddy's log since 2026-11-04 holds six 502s, all from the web container: EOF after 1–8 ms on scanner requests (rawgrab, a CONNECT tunnel probe, empty user agents). The idle gaps since the previous web response were 0.1–322 s, not near Node's 5 s, so they do not look like the same race. Not investigated further.

unattached_volume.inspection: read-only: docker volume inspect, container references, file metadata and catalog strings read with sudo; nothing mounted, started, changed or removed
unattached_volume.contents: a PostgreSQL 17 cluster initialised at 00:28:11 and last written at 00:28:56, with postmaster.pid still present (killed, not shut down); one database beyond the templates, 194 MB, named pathable in the WAL, holding alembic_version 0007_place_search and the dataset_versions and pilot_regions tables; 201 MB of WAL, which also holds the pathable_app role and SCRAM-SHA-256 verifiers
unattached_volume.identified_as: the throwaway database of restore.sh --into scratch, run on 2026-10-15 at 00:28 UTC
how: dockerd's journal: a container named pathable-restore-check-db joined network pathable-restore-check at 00:28:11.8 and ran 47.4 s; a second container joined that network at 00:28:28 and ran 30.9 s. Those are restore.sh's SCRATCH_DB, SCRATCH_NETWORK and its verifier.
0007_place_search was the schema on 2026-10-15; 0008 came on 2026-11-03.
restore.sh's next commit (6fa5132) is timestamped 00:29:15 UTC that night.
unattached_volume.why_it_remained: restore.sh starts the scratch container with docker run -d (no --rm) and removes it with docker rm -f (no -v). The postgis image declares /var/lib/postgresql/data a volume, so the scratch path leaves one anonymous volume behind each time it runs.
unattached_volume.action: none: deleting it is the founder's decision
